title: Constants and enums
summary: final, SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, and enums nested in Main.

say.never: A **constant** is a value that never changes, so it's marked `final`. `static` puts it on the class itself, so it must be written *outside* `main`, up near the top of the file. Capital letters with underscores tell every reader "this one never changes".
say.bit: A constant is a value that never changes. `static` makes it belong to the class, so it's declared **outside** `main`.

marks.label: belongs to the class, not one method

say.never: An **enum** is a type you invent yourself with a short, fixed list of allowed values. An `ALLIANCE` can only be `RED` or `BLUE`, and nothing else. If you misspell one, Java stops you right away, so typos can't sneak in.
say.bit: An **enum** is a type you invent with a fixed list of values. A variable of that type can only hold one of them, so typos are impossible.

say.never: Put both enums **inside** `Main`, near the constants, because only `Main` uses them. Careful with the curly braces: each `{` needs its own `}`.
say.bit: Both enums go **inside** `Main`, next to the constants, because only `Main` uses them.
